findings.title: The canon still gives incompatible rules for CJT breakdown
findings.introduced_by_change: The old unconditional rule remains; OD-A changes Appendix_B to require an explicit rule but does not reconcile the rest of the canon.
findings.impact: A board checker or lesson generator cannot derive one canon-backed breakdown rule. Implementations following different authoritative chapters can return different outcomes.
findings.recommended_action: Reconcile the unconditional statements with the explicit-rule requirement, or explicitly document which rule has precedence; keep runtime behavior unimplemented or openly qualified until resolved.

findings.title: XOR and XNOR have contradictory input-count rules
findings.introduced_by_change: The old XOR arity ambiguity survives; adding XNOR extends the same conflict to a new gate.
findings.impact: Appendix C permits two or more operands; the chapter and datasheet require two. For three active inputs, a parity XOR and the specified exactly-one predicate also diverge, so silently generalizing cannot preserve both interpretations.
findings.recommended_action: Specify whether XOR/XNOR are binary or variadic, and if variadic define their truth functions. Do not infer an owner choice from the two-input correction.

findings.title: The gain-3 example claims an exact observed result that its equation does not yield
findings.introduced_by_change: Pre-existing and byte-unchanged by OD-A; not an error introduced by the audited agent. It remains a defect in the book being pinned and inspected.
findings.impact: The text calls 3 an observed gain and says it is immune to forward-gain drift. Its formula gives 2.401921537229784 at A=12 and feedback=0.333, and 2.3094688221709005 at A=10. Including the displayed 1.5 evaluation stage gives 2.5736345438947668 at A=18, also not 3. The result could be copied into a validator or viewer as measured evidence despite being an approximation.
findings.recommended_action: Label the value as a limiting design approximation, use the finite-gain formula for the example, and distinguish predictions from actual recorded measurements.
